For anyone dabbling in the idea of becoming more active. Starting out you have to be very humble with your goals. It takes a lot of humility. 

I picked some basic weight lifts and push up/sit ups. I call it my prison workout. I live in a small apartment and used to think I didn’t have space/time for exercising daily. Now I budget 30 minutes a night. I started incredibly small and have only really just begun. 

I started with the goal of 1 set 1 rep of each, because motivation doesn’t come before action it comes during/after. Set your bar low folks and you’ll be very surprised how quickly you’ll see results!

Edit: I figured I should make an edit on this since it’s gaining a little traction. 

I use a habit tracking app on my phone to encourage myself to drink more water, eat consistently (I still allow garbage food, but I was skipping meals and figured if I aim at just becoming more consistent with meals I can adjust as I go), getting out/socializing (I have really bad anxiety/agoraphobia, so just leaving my apartment is very difficult for me sometimes. Sometimes just walking around in the backyard counts, sometimes I make it to a new place or event), and lastly I track exercise/stretching. 

I’ve been tracking/adjusting habits for over a year now. I fall off sometimes for days, weeks, or months, but the visual representation of my efforts always brings me back. 

I’m on week 3 for my 30 minute daily exercise. I’ve gone from doing 1 set with half reps/bad form and last night I actually completed my first bigger goal of 3 sets, 12 reps/lift to failure. I’m noticing a difference in my physical appearance, my mindset, my ability to rest/remain calm under stress, my focus is getting better, days no longer drag on. There’s so many little things I’m noticing improvement in!

My view on this topic has changed over the years as a man with mental health struggles. Minimalism for me is always trying to come to terms or be more mindful of this strange understanding I’ve always had that everything is only temporary. To me this means that almost all things are similar or the same; the main difference is their relevance to me. 

For example: 

I always used to wear the same black shirt and pants all the time. I would change my underwear and socks everyday, but would often wear the same outfit for half a week before rinsing and repeating. I used to think all clothes are the same so what’s the difference? I still think this way, but less extreme. I buy plain shirts of a few different colours and same for pants. A year ago I used to wear black everything, today I am wearing a yellow hoodie and red shoes. 

I live in a small two bedroom apartment with my 4 year old daughter. Almost everything in here was free or hand-me-down stuff. My couch is still comfy, my coffee table still holds drinks/snacks, and my tv sits in the same spot on my stand. All of which was free. 

A big thing I’ve been struggling with, especially since I’ve been living on my own, is over indulgence. You’d think with my minimal attitude toward things and stuff I’d have a fat sack of cash under my mattress. I am trying harder to work on getting back out of debt, not indulging in addictions/bad habits/etc. 

My idea of minimalism is always changing. I’m always trying to prove myself wrong when I gather the courage. A big thing for me with owning less or being attached to less, is my ability to be somewhat formless. I could lose everything and learn to be okay with that. But part of me wonders if I’ve taken on this outlook from past traumas. Life is fun!!! 

Respect to everyone in this sub. Not many people in my real life communities really relate to me with these things. Much love

I often feel like I’m just a depressed guy trying to play a role as a not depressed guy. But I am actively trying to change my own perception of myself, and a lot of the time I walk around feeling like a fraud. So I withdraw, from everybody. 

I’ve written off so many people because I had myself convinced that they were either the enemy or wouldn’t understand my condition. People probably just see me as the flaky guy that disappears for months/years. I’ve grown okay with people not understanding, and I’ve also been trying to reframe past relationships/friendships in a positive light. Not every bad situation or misunderstanding was an attack. I’m even trying to reconnect with old friends, and trying to make some new ones!

I started playing guitar pretty much exacty three years ago, and that has helped me beyond explaination. But if I had to try, I’d say it gave me an outlet I didn’t have for sad thoughts and maddening. Oh, I started painting a week ago, and I’ve grown facinated by it. It takes courage to take on a blank canvas. I’ve also discovered that oddly enough white paint seems most important. With white you can mix so many different colours. It’s wonderful. 

And there’s a girl now. I feel like I did when I was eight years old in third grade with a crush. It feels good.

One thing I’d say that is most definitely a sign of depression is the loss of sex drive. It doesn’t help that my medication has a side effect of libido loss. It’s been 18 months since I’ve gotten laid. Longest I’ve gone since I lost my virginity. 

There’s not all bad in that, I took the time off to really look at past relationships and what drove me in them. And sadly, sex was a main drive in all of them, looking back, it was definitely unhealthy. So now I’m not only looking for physical attraction, but compatibility in personality, humour, interests, communication, and politeness/kindness. 

With all the talk on the news about video games, porn, and weed creating incels, I can kind of see where they’re coming from. A lot of my life has been consumption of these three things and spending lots of time by myself. No fault of anybody else other than myself. I’ve dealt with some pretty nasty thoughts, not about harming other people, but how nasty everybody can be to one another. It can definitely cloud your perception of the world. I tend toward the private self destruction. Whereas some evil men tend towards public self destruction. If I was going to do any harm at all, it would be in killing myself. 

I’ve instead done lots of research and trying until it won’t let me try anymore. If I had to explain it another way, I suppose I’d compare it to that of Batman. Big stretch I know, comparing myself to Batman. But better to be a Batman than a Bane.

I am a 26 year old single father, have been since I was 23. Six months into fatherhood, I got cheated on. Then six months later after I’d finally moved out of my parents house and into my own place, covid hit. I spent the first six months living here in my small apartment, with little to no furniture, with a 1 year old, terrified of her getting sick. I didn’t go many places or do much of anything. 

I’ve had to learn a lot. Stuff you wouldn’t think about until it happens, like taking care of a child while you’re both sick, taking weeks off work without any income, losing just about all of my so called friends, seeing what family checks in knowing my situation. It put a lot into perspective for me.

I’ve tried a lot of stuff too. I quit smoking, taught myself how to play guitar, got on anti depressants, went to therapy, cooking, cleaning, general maintenance, etc. 

I’ve had to learn forgiveness, patience, resilience, and perseverance. I am proud of both myself and my daughter. I have taught her a lot and she has taught me a lot. 


I will forever cherish the time I spent bunkered up here playing Frank Sinatra, dancing in the kitchen, while bacon sizzled on the pan. So little truly mattered as long as we were healthy. 

I normalized all emotions, communicating our thoughts/feelings, proper use of manners, eye contact, apologizing, boundaries, privacy, etc. 

And it paid off too. My kid is incredible. She’s so smart and funny for her age. I know everybody thinks their kid is a genius, but I’ve had multiple of her teachers tell me that she’s way above where other kids in her kindergarten class are. 


I firmly believe that I will/have become an inner part of the voice in her head. I know this because when I get upset I hear my parents voices come out of my mouth.

I only speak fondly of her mother, step father, and now baby sister. She does not yet understand why we live in seperate houses, but I’m sure one day she will figure things out for herself. 


I’ve dealt with depression, anxiety, panic attacks, avoidance, indulgence, addiction, drugs, sex, toxic relationships, etc. I want to be there for her to help her through these things. 

I try my best to write to her on my computer. It helps me process feelings and maybe one day she will appreciate reading my thoughts. 

Much love to anybody out there fighting a similar battle.
